title: Railroad Time
dek: Four sourced turning points. Speak or type a clue and the line moves. The room does not call a model and does not write to the network.
body:
Railroad Time is a speakable history room at /railroads. Four curated eras sit on one line: 1825, when Locomotion No. 1 hauled an opening train on the Stockton & Darlington; 1869, when Chinese workers built the Central Pacific through the Sierra and were crowded out of the Promontory photograph; 1883, when the railroads adopted standard time and some towns had two noons; and 1964, when the Tokaido Shinkansen made high speed an ordinary public service between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka.

Ask about beginnings, builders, time, or speed. Keyword routing picks one of those four answers. Speech recognition and speech synthesis run in the browser, and only after an explicit tap. A typed question is always there. The plates are generated historical interpretations, not documentary photographs, and each era names its source.

The room stores visited era ids in this tab only. It does not call a live model, and it does not write to the network.
